text.p: Australia on Friday welcomed the appointment of one of its top diplomats as executive chairman of the U.N. commission in charge of Iraqi disarmament.

Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said in a statement that the choice of Canberra's U.N. ambassador for the post "is testimony to Australia's high international standing in the field of arms control and non-proliferation".

U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan earlier named Butler to replace Sweden's Rolf Ekeus as head of the U.N. Special Commission, known as UNSCOM. Ekeus expects to leave in July to become Sweden's ambassador to Washington.
Downer said Butler, a career diplomat who has held several important posts, had excellent credentials for his new job.

Butler, 54, known for his articulate and occasionally blunt comments, has been involved in disarmament affairs since 1983, when he was appointed Australia's first ambassador at the Geneva-based Conference on Disarmament for five years.

He was also convenor of Australia's Canberra Commission for the abolition of nuclear weapons, a committee of prominent international figures which drew up recommendations for ridding the world of nuclear arms. Downer's office would not comment on Butler's likely replacement in New York.
Australia's conservative government, elected in March 1996, after 13 years in opposition, has appointed several of its political heavyweights to key overseas posts.
Analysts expect Butler to be replaced by a senior diplomat.
